claims.claim: Leo called the 449 meeting one not of judges but of robbers
claims.witness: Leo, letter to Pulcheria (npnf212 l.8640)

claims.claim: Theodosius II died in 450 and Marcian succeeded
claims.witness: Driver and Hodgson introduction, after Bethune-Baker (driver-hodgson l.303-305); Zachariah II, end (zachariah l.2034-2036, 2053-2054)

claims.claim: The council was brought together by Leo's exertion and his letter to Marcian and Pulcheria
claims.witness: Zachariah III.1 (zachariah l.2078-2081)

claims.claim: Pulcheria ordered the governor of Bithynia to clear the city of disorderly clerics, monks and laymen
claims.witness: Hefele III, sec. 185 (hefele v3 l.14989-15000)

claims.claim: The council's letter to Leo speaks of 520 priests
claims.witness: Letter XCVIII, from the Synod to Leo (npnf212 l.8753); Hefele: only in the Greek text (hefele v3 l.15786)

claims.claim: The chronicle known as Zachariah's counts 567 bishops
claims.witness: Zachariah II end and III preface (zachariah l.2038-2039, 2077-2078)

claims.claim: Leo speaks of about 600; the usual reckoning with representatives is 630; the lists of those present are incomplete
claims.witness: Hefele III, sec. 188 (hefele v3 l.15720-15748)

claims.claim: All present were Greeks and Easterns except the Roman legates and two Africans, Aurelius of Adrumetum and Rusticianus
claims.witness: Hefele III, sec. 188 (hefele v3 l.15749-15756)

claims.claim: The judges asked whether Flavian had kept the faith; the legates, Anatolius, Maximus and others said he had; the Illyrians cried, we all have erred, let us all be pardoned
claims.witness: Acts, Session I (npnf214 l.19224-19268)

claims.claim: Dioscorus said, I receive the of two; the two I do not receive
claims.witness: Acts, Session I (npnf214 l.19254-19260)

claims.claim: The bishops cried that no one makes another exposition; no new exposition in writing
claims.witness: Acts, Session II (npnf214 l.19316-19344)

claims.claim: The creeds of Nicaea and Constantinople, Cyril's letters to Nestorius and to John, and Leo's Tome were read
After the Tome the bishops cried, Peter has spoken thus through Leo; Leo and Cyril taught the same thing; these are the things Dioscorus hid away
claims.witness: Acts, Session II (npnf214 l.19996-20007)

claims.claim: The Tome says each form does the acts which belong to it in communion with the other; the one shines out in miracles, the other succumbs to injuries
claims.witness: The Tome as read at Chalcedon (npnf214 l.19797-19801)

claims.claim: Dioscorus, thrice summoned, did not come, and was deposed on 13 October
claims.witness: Sentence sent to Dioscorus, Session III (npnf214 l.20049-20052, 20082-20090)

claims.claim: The legates' sentence says Leo, through them and the synod, with Peter, stripped Dioscorus of the episcopate
claims.witness: Acts, Session III (npnf214 l.20055-20064)

claims.claim: In Session IV, 161 bishops gave separate opinions that the Tome agreed with Nicaea and Constantinople, and the rest assented together
claims.witness: Acts, Session IV (npnf214 l.20123-20135)

claims.claim: In Session V the legates threatened to leave for a synod in the West if the bishops did not agree to Leo's letter; a committee was imposed by the emperor
claims.witness: Acts, Session V with Percival's summary (npnf214 l.20142-20153)

claims.claim: The judges asked: which would you follow, the most holy Leo or Dioscorus? and ordered that two natures united unchangeably, inseparably, unconfusedly be added
claims.witness: Acts, Session V (npnf214 l.20165-20178)

claims.claim: The Definition confesses one and the same Christ in two natures, unconfusedly, immutably, indivisibly, inseparably, united in one person and subsistence, and receives Cyril's letters and Leo's Tome
claims.witness: Definition of Faith (npnf214 l.20255-20298)

claims.claim: The Definition forbids any different faith, on pain of deposition or anathema
claims.witness: Definition of Faith (npnf214 l.20299-20312)

claims.claim: The original reading was 'in two natures'; the present Greek has 'of two natures'
claims.witness: Hefele, note to the Definition (npnf214 l.20359-20415)

claims.claim: Marcian attended Session VI in person; the bishops acclaimed him and Pulcheria; he made Chalcedon a metropolis in name
claims.witness: Acts, Session VI (npnf214 l.20470-20491)

claims.claim: Anatolius wrote that the bishops placed the definition on the altar of Euphemia and handed it to Marcian and Pulcheria
claims.witness: Anatolius to Leo, note to the Definition (npnf214 l.20322-20353)

claims.claim: Session VII assigned the three Palestines to Jerusalem and the two Phoenicias and Arabia to Antioch, by agreement of Juvenal and Maximus
claims.witness: Decree, Session VII (npnf214 l.20500-20511)

claims.claim: Theodoret was made to anathematize Nestorius and said he had subscribed the definition and Leo's letter
claims.witness: Acts as Blomfield Jackson quotes them (npnf203 l.3310-3337)

claims.claim: Canon 28 gave Constantinople privileges equal to old Rome and rank next after her, and the ordination of the metropolitans of Pontus, Asia and Thrace
claims.witness: Canon XXVIII (npnf214 l.22216-22240)

claims.claim: In Session XVI the canon was read with 192 signatures; 350 had signed the definition a week before; Lucentius protested that the bishops had been circumvented
claims.witness: Acts, Session XVI with Percival's notes (npnf214 l.22578-22647)

claims.claim: Leo wrote to Pulcheria that by Peter's authority he absolutely dis-annuls the bishops' assents against the Nicene canons
Dioscorus was sent to Gangra in Paphlagonia and Proterius appointed to Alexandria
claims.witness: Evagrius II.5 (walford l.3363-3367); Zachariah III.1 (zachariah l.2081-2083)

claims.claim: Priscus, quoted by Evagrius, says a crowd in Alexandria drove the troops into the old temple of Serapis and burned them alive
claims.witness: Evagrius II.5 (walford l.3372-3382)

claims.claim: Monks who had been at the council roused Palestine, and its opponents made Theodosius bishop of Jerusalem
claims.witness: Evagrius II.5 (walford l.3405-3420); Zachariah III, chapter list (zachariah l.2094-2107)

claims.claim: The chronicle known as Zachariah's says the council introduced the heresy of Nestorius and tore the robe of Christ into ten thousand rents
claims.witness: Zachariah III.1 (zachariah l.2176-2186)

claims.claim: Book III of the chronicle is drawn from Zachariah's Greek history, which ended in 491; the Syriac compiler is another man
claims.witness: Hamilton and Brooks, introduction (zachariah l.300-318)

claims.claim: Evagrius copied the decree of Chalcedon somewhat more than a hundred years after the council
claims.witness: Hefele, note to the Definition (npnf214 l.20396-20399)

claims.claim: Severus of Antioch anathematized the things done at Chalcedon
claims.witness: Severus, Select Letters VI, part 2 (severus book6 part2 l.1349-1350, 1518)

claims.claim: Timothy Aelurus's refutation of Chalcedon and of Leo's Tome is held only in Classical Armenian
claims.witness: timothy-aelurus file header (l.1-9)

claims.claim: The Church of the East's Synodicon includes the canons of the council at Chalcedon, Leo's letter to Flavian against Eutyches and the Fathers' testimonies appended to it; Mar Aba's synod of 544 cites the synod of the 567 bishops at Chalcedon
claims.witness: Synodicon orientale, Chabot's list and notes (chabot l.1083-1113, 36874-36877)

claims.claim: Chabot says the Church of the East accepted Chalcedon in so far as it condemned Eutyches
claims.witness: Chabot, note (chabot l.36950-36951)

claims.claim: Wigram found the Definition in the Mosul manuscript of the Synodicon, with blessed Cyril altered to accursed and the phrase on Nestorius's folly omitted, which he judges a later copyist's change
claims.witness: Wigram, ch. XI (wigram l.14620-14640)

claims.claim: Chalcedon was rejected absolutely by Egypt and Palestine, by a large majority of the Christians of the Antiochene patriarchate and by the Armenian church; its problems remain causes of schism while Armenian, Copt and Jacobite remain unreconciled
claims.witness: Wigram, ch. VIII (wigram l.7126-7159)

claims.claim: Armenia took no part: the councils on Eutyches met without her knowledge, and Chalcedon met after Avarayr, with her bishops imprisoned or exiled
claims.witness: Ormanian, ch. VIII (ormanian l.2444-2463)

claims.claim: A synod at Dvin in 506 under Babken rejected the acts of Chalcedon; a synod at Dvin in 554 under Nerses II confirmed it
claims.witness: Ormanian, ch. VIII (ormanian l.2499-2511, 2549-2556)

claims.claim: The Greek and Latin churches came to recognise Chalcedon as the fourth ecumenical council; the Armenian Church would have nothing to do with it
claims.witness: Ormanian, ch. VIII (ormanian l.2517-2522)

contested_claims.claim: How many bishops attended
contested_claims.sides: The council's letter to Leo: 520 (Greek text only, Hefele); the chronicle known as Zachariah's: 567; Leo, by Hefele's report: about 600; the usual reckoning Hefele gives: 630; Percival: 350 signed the definition

contested_claims.claim: Whether the Definition said 'in two natures' or 'of two natures'
contested_claims.sides: The present Greek text: 'of two natures'; the old Latin: 'in two natures'; Hefele argues from Euthymius, Severus of Antioch, Evagrius, the 553 conference and Leontius that 'in two natures' was original, and the Session V debate supports him

contested_claims.claim: Why Dioscorus was deposed
contested_claims.sides: The sentence: for disregard of the canons, disobedience and other crimes, having thrice refused to come (acts); the chronicle known as Zachariah's: because he said Christ became incarnate from two natures and two natures should not be confessed after the union; it has Anatolius say he was deposed not for the faith but for refusing communion with Leo (zachariah l.2314-2325)

contested_claims.claim: Whether the bishops signed canon 28 freely
contested_claims.sides: Lucentius, Leo's legate: they were circumvented and forced to sign; the bishops: no one was forced; Aëtius of Constantinople: done openly and according to the canons

contested_claims.claim: Who brought the council about
contested_claims.sides: The Definition: the command of Marcian and Valentinian; Hefele: Marcian, with Pulcheria; the chronicle known as Zachariah's: the exertion of Leo and his letter to Marcian and Pulcheria

contested_claims.claim: How the Church of the East stood to Chalcedon
contested_claims.sides: Chabot: it accepted the council in so far as it condemned Eutyches; Wigram: it received Chalcedon and the Tome as orthodox, though the Syriac Definition calls Cyril accursed, likely a copyist's change; Ormanian: the Nestorians prided themselves on Chalcedon's authority (ormanian l.2486-2490)

contested_claims.claim: When Armenia first rejected Chalcedon
contested_claims.sides: Ormanian: at Dvin in 506, confirmed at Dvin in 554; the tree's Armenian census entry: formally at Dvin in 554
